paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the struggle you feel is not a sign that something is wrong with God's law. Paul says the law is spiritual and good (Romans 7:14, 16). He also says that in his inner being he delights in God's law (Romans 7:22). So the wanting is real, and the wanting is good.

Now here's the hard part, and Paul doesn't dress it up. He says, "For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do" (Romans 7:19). He sees another law at work in his body, warring against the law of his mind (Romans 7:23). If you've ever set your own alarm and then fought your own thumb, you're in good company, and Paul is the one who invited you in.

So where does the war end? Paul cries out, "What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?" and then the answer comes right behind it: "Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord!" (Romans 7:24, 25). Rescue doesn't come from trying harder, it comes from Jesus. I sat in the back of a drawer thinking I was done, and I couldn't climb out on my own either, so I'm telling you this one from the heart. Be honest about the struggle, keep delighting in God's Word, and keep your eyes on the One who rescues.
